texts.preamble: M/S. Kamadhenu Food Products vs The Head (O[/Mie/Ie) Division on 4 February, 2026 2026:Ker:9634 In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr.Justice Ziyad Rahman A.A. Wednesday, The 4Th Day Of February 2026 / 15Th Magha, 1947 Wp(C) No. 28817 Of 2015 Petitioner: M/S. Kamadhenu Food Products Represented By A.S. Sreejith, Proprietor, Shed No. 10, Mini Industrial Estate, Kanniyampuram, Ottapalam, Palakkad District. Residing At 10/330, Srivilas, Kanniyampuram Post, Ottapala, Palakkad District-679104. By Adv Sri.K.Ravi (Pariyarath) Respondents: 1 The Head (Ip/Mie/Ie) Division Kerala Small Industries Development Corporation, Ppo No. 50, Housing Board Building Santhi Nagar, Thiruvananthapuram-695001. 2 Estate Manager, Sidco Industrial Estate Karakkad, Shoranur-2, Palakkad District. By Adv Sri.R.T.Pradeep, S.C. This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission On 04.02.2026, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following: 2026:Ker:9634 Wp(C) No. 28817 Of 2015 2 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner is a proprietary concern, which is conducting an industrial unit manufacturing Vermicelli and allied food products at Mini Industrial Estate, Kanniyampuram, Ottapalam. The dispute involved in this writ petition pertains to the notice of termination issued by the 2nd respondent and the notice of eviction issued, directing the petitioner to vacate the building where the proprietary concern is housed. The Mini Industrial Estate, where the petitioner is running its business belongs to the Kerala State Small Industries Development Corporation. 2. Earlier, one N.Suryanarayanan was allotted with the building, which is the subject matter of the dispute. Thereafter, the said Suryanarayanan entered into a partnership deed with one A.S. Sidharthan, the father of the 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 proprietor of the petitioner firm. is the deed of partnership entered into between the parties. Ext . P2 is the Articles of Agreement entered into between the Kerala State Small Industries Development & Employment Corporation Ltd. (SIDCO) with the said N.Suryanarayanan as well as Sri.A.S. Sidharthan, for the purpose of allotment of the said building for running M/s.Kamadhenu Food Products. On the basis of the same, the said partnership firm was running its business in the building and later, as per Ext.P3 the partnership was reconstituted by which, the said Suryanarayanan exited from the partnership and it was being continued as a proprietary concern of Sri.A.S. Sidharthan. The said Sidharthan passed away on 14.10.2005 and thereafter, the son of the said Sidharthan is continuing the said establishment in the said building. Ext.P8 termination notice was issued by the 1st respondent on 14.11.2014 stating that, the petitioner is in 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 unauthorized occupation of the building, as the allotment of the building stands in the name of Sri.N. Suryanarayanan, who is no more. Even though the petitioner submitted Ext.P9 in response to Ext.P8, Ext.P10 order was issued by the 1 st respondent reiterating the stand taken in Ext.P8. Based on Ext.P10, Ext.P11 notice was also issued intimating that, the petitioner will be evicted on 25.09.2015. It was in these circumstances this writ petition is submitted alleging Exts.P8, P10 and P11.
texts.arguments: 4. The main contention raised by the learned Counsel for the petitioner is that, Exts.P8, P10 and P11 were issued without properly considering the documents available on record. It is pointed out that, Ext.P8 was issued by the 1 st 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 respondent stating that, the allotment was made to Sri.N. Suryanarayanan and he is no more. On the other hand, the learned Counsel for the petitioner, by placing reliance upon Ext.P2, which is the articles of agreement, entered into between the SIDCO on one side and the said Suryanarayanan and said Sidharthan on the other side, would contend that the said documents clearly indicate that, a contractual relationship was created by the SIDCO, with respect to the allotment of the said property with the said Sidharthan as well, who is the father of the proprietor of the petitioner firm herein. The petitioner is even now functioning in the very same name even though the constitution of the same 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 was changed to that of a proprietary concern, consequent to the retirement of one of the earlier partners. The fact that, the name of Sri.A.S. Sidharthan, the predecessor in interest of the petitioner, is mentioned in Ext.P2 agreement in which the 1st respondent is a party, is something very crucial and the said fact is also not seen referred to in Ext.P8 termination 2026:KER:9634 WP(C) NO. 28817 OF 2015 notice.
